record.paper_title: Resolution of Some Open Problems Concerning Multiple Zeta Evaluations of Arbitrary Depth
record.original_question: Is the Riemann zeta value ζ(5) irrational; equivalently, does ζ(5) fail to lie in Q[Z_1] = Q?

evidence.quote: For example, there is as yet no proof that z(5) ∉ Q[Z1] = Q, although it is strongly suspected that z(5) is indeed irrational.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{-s}$ denote the Riemann zeta function for $\mathrm{Re}(s) > 1$. Determine whether $\zeta(5) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^5}$ is irrational, i.e., prove or disprove that $\zeta(5) \notin \mathbb{Q}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The irrationality of ζ(5) remains an open problem. Apéry (1978) proved ζ(3) is irrational, and Ball–Rivoal (2001) showed infinitely many odd zeta values are irrational. Zudilin (2001) proved at least one of ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational, but no individual odd zeta value beyond ζ(3) has been proven irrational.

status_evidence.title: Zudilin: One of ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that at least one of the numbers ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational.
status_evidence.claim: The irrationality of ζ(5) individually is not known; only a 'one-of-four' result exists.

status_evidence.title: Rivoal: La fonction zêta de Riemann prend une infinité de valeurs irrationnelles aux entiers impairs
status_evidence.snippet: Infinitely many of the values ζ(2k+1) are irrational.
status_evidence.claim: Only infinitely-many-type results are known; ζ(5) is not individually known to be irrational.
